t: You're standing near the site of the old Shaftesbury Theatre, which stood here from 1888 until 1941. It was built by John Lancaster for his wife, Ellen Wallis, a well-known Shakespearean actress. The architect was C. J. Phipps, who designed more than forty theatres in the later nineteenth century. The builders were Patman and Fotheringham, and it cost twenty thousand pounds. It opened on 20 October 1888 with a production of As You Like It, which suits a house made for a Shakespearean actress.
